blocks.text: Intermolecular forces are also considered as binding forces just like chemical bonds. However, the attraction between the molecules is much weaker than the chemical bonds. These forces are believed to exist between all kinds of atoms and molecules when they are sufficiently close to each other. Such intermolecular forces are called van der Waals forces. These intermolecular forces bring the molecules close together and give particular physical properties to the substances in gaseous, liquid, and solid states.
Three types of such forces are mentioned here:

items: Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces or London dispersion forces

blocks.text: The detailed discussion on these forces will be made in the chapter on states and phases of matter.
